violation_type.title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance (26 TAC §746.2803(4))
violation_type.short_title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance
violation_type.typical_finding: Information gathered by the CCI through interview and observation on 7/17/2023 showed that several children stated a caregiver was pulling their arm and it's hurting them.

finding_variants.text: Information gathered by the CCI through interview and observation on 7/17/2023 showed that several children stated a caregiver was pulling their arm and it's hurting them.
A caregiver failed to use positive methods of discipline and guidance when she struck a child using her hand.

This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation. Based on information obtained during a DFPS investigation, a caregiver was observed snatching toys from children, throwing or slamming items down in the classroom and kicking a chair.
During the course of the investigation, it was determined staff used statements focused on negative behavior when children don't listen or participate in activity as directed by caregiver.

Based on the information obtained during the investigation, it was determined that the operation was non-compliant with this standard as a caregiver wrote on a child's face with a marker as a form of discipline.

This standard was reviewed in relation to the DFPS investigation and was found to be deficient. The employee did not use a positive method of guidance when the child was pulled by the arm to move the child to the desired location by the caregiver. The caregiver is no longer employed at the operation.

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance: This standard was evaluated regarding an investigation, and a violation was found. The caregiver did not encourage self-esteem, self-control, and self-direction during the discipline of children. The caregiver did not redirect behavior using positive statements. When children were overly active in the classroom, the caregiver grabbed and pulled on them instead of using positive statements to redirect the behaviors. In addition, this action did not teach children acceptable behavior and self-control. The caregiver did not teach children self-direction when the caregivers in the classroom withheld young children with challenging behaviors in a specific area without having access to active play or independent movement.
